record.original_question: Does every bounded C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space have a bounded rational calculus?

evidence.quote: Problem 28 (Rational calculus and contractivity). (i) Does every bounded C0 -semigroup on a Hilbert space have a bounded rational calculus?
Comments. The answer to the first question is no.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ be a bounded $C_0$-semigroup on $H$, with infinitesimal generator $-A$ (so that $T(t)=e^{-tA}$). Let $\mathrm{Rat}_b(\mathbb{C}_+)$ denote the algebra of bounded rational functions on the open right half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\mathrm{Re}\,z>0\}$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|r\|_\infty=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{C}_+}|r(z)|$. For such $r$ (whose poles lie in the closed left half-plane, hence in the resolvent set of $A$), the operator $r(A)\in\mathcal{B}(H)$ is defined by the usual rational functional calculus. One says that $A$ admits a \emph{bounded rational calculus} if there exists a constant $C\ge 0$ such that
$$\|r(A)\|_{\mathcal{B}(H)} \le C\,\|r\|_\infty \qquad \text{for every } r\in\mathrm{Rat}_b(\mathbb{C}_+).$$
Question: Does every bounded $C_0$-semigroup on a Hilbert space have a bounded rational calculus in the above sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is reported to have a negative answer: not every bounded $C_0$-semigroup on a Hilbert space admits a bounded rational calculus. Counterexamples in this circle of ideas include bounded (and even bounded analytic) Hilbert-space semigroups that are not similar to contraction semigroups, and sectorial operators on Hilbert space with bounded imaginary powers but without bounded $H^\infty$-calculus, which obstruct a uniform rational calculus bound.

status_evidence.title: Functional calculus for a bounded C_0-semigroup on Hilbert space
status_evidence.snippet: Functional calculus results for negative generators of bounded C0-semigroups on Hilbert space, identifying the algebras that act boundedly.
status_evidence.claim: Studies bounded functional calculi for generators of bounded C0-semigroups on Hilbert spaces, locating the precise (Besov/A(C+)) algebra of symbols.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples concerning powers of sectorial operators on a Hilbert space
status_evidence.snippet: Operators on Hilbert space with bounded imaginary powers but without bounded H-infinity calculus on the corresponding sector.
status_evidence.claim: Provides Hilbert-space counterexamples showing functional calculi need not be bounded, used to negate a bounded rational calculus.

status_evidence.title: A Bounded Compact Semigroup on Hilbert Space not Similar to a Contraction One
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a bounded C0-semigroup on Hilbert space that is not similar to a contraction semigroup.
status_evidence.claim: A bounded C0-semigroup on Hilbert space need not be similar to a contraction semigroup, an obstruction relevant to bounded rational calculus.
